Cost and Energy Analysis Next, we built a technoeconomic, or lifecycle analysis, model of the Fz-CVD reactor to test its commercial viability. For our base case we assume a 260 mm diameter boule to make M10 wafers. The poly-Si growth rate ranged from 100 µm/min to 300 µm/min for the Fz-CVD process. For reference, we note that the effective growth rate for the traditional Siemens + Cz method to produce an M10 boule is about 750 µm/min considering heating/cooling cycles, product harvesting, and consumable parts replacement. The potentially lower silicon growth rate for the Fz-CVD process comes with lower energy costs per kg of silicon produced and fewer consumable and maintenance costs. The largest economic lever is the higher quality (longer lifetime) wafer which not only increases efficiency in the final cells but also allows for much lower degradation rates and therefore longer service life, reducing the system- level LCOE.
